paper.title: MA-EgoQA: Question Answering over Egocentric Videos from Multiple Embodied Agents

latest_version.version_label: arXiv v2 (HTML full text) reviewed on 2026-08-30

evidence.page: arXiv HTML full text, Section 3 and 3.3
evidence.figure_or_table: Figure 3 (statistics across days, agents and categories)
evidence.paraphrase: 1,741 multiple-choice questions built over 266 hours of synchronised egocentric video from six people sharing a house for seven days. Each question is written so that it cannot be answered from a single stream: answering requires aggregating information from more than two agents, forcing a system-level global memory across parallel long-horizon streams.

evidence.page: arXiv HTML full text, Sections 3 and 4.1
evidence.paraphrase: Five categories - social interaction, task coordination, theory of mind, temporal reasoning and environmental interaction - are evaluated in five-option multiple-choice format. Multi-span questions require reasoning over several non-contiguous temporal windows, testing long-horizon recall and temporal ordering rather than single-clip perception.

Sixteen video and long-video baselines plus the EgoMAS memory baseline are compared; the paper reports that current approaches fail to handle multiple egocentric streams, isolating cross-agent memory construction rather than per-video understanding as the bottleneck.

adjudication_notes: A separate architecture record (egomas.json, EgoMAS) is created under counting_rules.md because the same paper contributes both a benchmark and a distinct memory architecture.
